sources.entry: sqlglot - A no-dependency SQL parser, transpiler, optimizer, and engine.

summary.one_liner: SQLGlot is a no-dependency Python SQL parser, transpiler, optimizer, and engine that translates queries between over 30 SQL dialects.
keywords: find tables and columns in query
summary.what_it_does: SQLGlot parses SQL into an expression tree and generates SQL back out for a target dialect, covering over 30 dialects such as DuckDB, Presto/Trino, Spark/Databricks, Snowflake, and BigQuery. It can format SQL, translate identifiers, data types, functions, and time formats between dialects, and preserve comments on a best-effort basis. It can detect syntax errors such as unbalanced parentheses and report dialect incompatibilities as warnings or errors depending on configuration. The optimizer rewrites queries into a canonical form, using schema information where provided. Other capabilities include programmatic SQL building, tree transformation, AST diffing, metadata lookup such as finding columns and tables, and a small Python engine that executes SQL over dictionaries.
use_cases: migrate Snowflake or Spark SQL to another warehouse
find tables and columns referenced in a query
validate SQL syntax in a pipeline
run SQL against Python objects for unit tests
how_to_run: pip3 install "sqlglot[c]"  # optional mypyc-compiled version, Python 3.10+
notable: Pure Python with no required dependencies
Transpiles between more than 30 SQL dialects, with support levels marked Official, Community, or Plugin
Optional mypyc-compiled build that the README says is roughly 3-5x faster
Plugin system that lets third-party packages register new dialects through entry points
Can execute SQL over in-memory Python dictionaries
caveats: The parser is intentionally lenient and may accept SQL that a real engine rejects; it is not a validator
Subclassing dialects may not work with the sqlglot[c] compiled install, so custom dialects may need the pure Python version
Some translations are best-effort and may emit warnings or be incomplete; the README says coverage improves over time
The project accepts pull requests only from maintainers; outside contributions are limited to issues
Plugin dialects are not maintained by the core team
